normal: are round with a smooth, flat surface and have centered, unlit wicks. They appear uniformly white and are housed in circular metal containers.
chunk-of-wax-missing: presence of small holes or pits on any part of the candle's surface, excluding the edges. The anomaly should be localized on the round hole or pit area only
damaged-corner-of-packaging: small chips or pits located specifically along the edges of the candle. The anomaly should be localized on the chipped edge area only
different-colour-spot: presence of visible stains or discolorations on the surface of the candle, as indicated by red spots or marks that deviate from the uniform color. The anomaly should be localized on the discolored spot area only
foreign-particals-on-candle: presence of foreign particles or debris embedded on the surface of the candle, which may appear as dirt or specks disrupting the smooth texture. The anomaly should be localized on the foreign particle area only
wax-melded-out-of-the-candle: irregular smears or deformations on the surface of the candle, particularly evident by streaks or uneven texture. The anomaly should be localized on the smeared area only

normal: smooth, uniform surface, free of any air bubbles, dark spots, scratches, or deformations. The capsules exhibit consistent coloring and are correctly shaped.
bubble: presence of air bubble within the capsule. The anomaly should be localized on the bubble only
bubble-discolor: presence of a dark spot in one capsule. The anomaly should be localized on the dark spot area only
bubble-discolor-scratch: presence of a scratch marks on the surface of one of the capsules. The anomaly should be localized on the scratch area only
bubble-discolor-scratch-leak: presence of leakage of encapsulated material or punctures, squeezing, or structural deformities in a capsule. The anomaly should be localized on the leakage or deformity area only

normal: a smooth, crescent-shaped surface with a uniform beige color and no visible irregularities or damage. It displays a consistent texture and retains its characteristic curved form without any marks or defects.
burnt: slightly darker or blackened spot on the surface of the cashew. The anomaly should be localized on that burnt spot only
same-colour-spot: a small, subtle patch on the cashew that is slightly different in color but blends closely with the natural hue. The anomaly should be localized on that similar-colour spot only
corner-or-edge-breakage: section of the cashew nut's edge is visibly missing or chipped off. The anomaly should be localized on the chipped edge area only
small-hole: a small, pretty deep, circular hole can be seen, piercing through the nut. The anomaly should be localized on the hole itself only
small-scratches: tiny, fine lines or scratches that don't penetrate deeply but may be challenging to observe against the beige background. The anomaly should be localized on the scratched area only

normal: has a smooth, even surface with uniform edges and corners. It exhibits a consistent color and texture throughout, with no visible cracks, chunks missing, or discolorations. The overall appearance is polished and symmetrical
chunk-of-gum-missing: noticeable indentation or cavity in the middle of the chewing gum, leading to an uneven texture. The anomaly should be localized on the missing chunk area only
chunk-of-gum-missing_small-cracks: combination of a chunk missing and several fine cracks radiating from the missing part. The anomaly should be localized on both the missing chunk and the cracked area only
corner-missing: small section missing from one of the corners, giving the gum an irregular corner shape. The anomaly should be localized on the chipped corner area only
similar-colour-spot: small, subtle spot on the gum's surface, with a slightly different texture or color, making it look like a minor blemish. The anomaly should be localized on that similar-colour spot only

normal: A perfect fryum with no visible irregularities, breakages, or color spots, maintaining its intended uniform shape and color.
different-colour-spot: presence of irregular color patches on the fryum. These spots can vary widely in color from darker hues like red to lighter shades similar to the fryum's base color. The anomaly should be localized on the discolored spot area only
fryum-stuck-together: two individual fryums become inseparably fused together. It results in an irregular, combined shape that deviates from the typical singular form of a fryum. The anomaly should be localized on the area where the fryums are stuck together only
middle-breakage: crack or break within the structure of the fryum. The break can be seen as a distinct separation or gap disrupting the uniformity of the fryum. The anomaly should be localized on the broken area only

normal: depict typical elbow macaroni pasta pieces, which appear to be well-formed and consistent in shape. They exhibit a smooth, curved surface with a uniform golden-yellow color.
chip-around-edge-and-corner: small piece missing from the edge of the macaroni, giving it an uneven contour. It's typically noticeable at the outermost part of the curved surface. The anomaly should be localized on the chipped edge area only
different-colour-spot: presence of a distinct reddish or purplish spot on one or more macaroni pieces. The spot contrasts noticeably with the natural color of the macaroni. The anomaly should be localized on the discolored spot area only
middle-breakage-small-scratches: noticeable hole or breakage in the middle part of the macaroni. It disrupts the regular cylindrical shape and creates a void that is evident when viewed from any angle. The anomaly should be localized on the broken area only
similar-colour-spots: a spot that blends in with the macaroni's natural hue, making it harder to detect at first glance. The spot usually appears slightly darker or lighter but maintains a similar color tone to the surrounding pasta. The anomaly should be localized on that similar-colour spot only
small-cracks: fine, linear cracks or scratches along the surface of the macaroni. These imperfections are generally shallow but can be observed running along the length or circumference of the piece. The anomaly should be localized on the scratched area only

normal: the macaroni pieces exhibit a smooth and uniform yellowish color throughout. The edges are neatly rounded without any chips or cracks. There are no discolored spots or surface scratches present. Each piece maintains a consistent shape and texture with a slightly glossy finish.
color-spot-similar-to-the-object: a spot that blends with the macaroni's natural yellowish color, creating a lighter, whitish or yellowish patch. These spots are subtle and may almost merge with the macaroni's surface tone. The anomaly should be localized on that small, subtle similar colour spot only
different-color-spot: a discolored area with a dark or purplish tint on one or more macaroni pieces. These spots stand out against the natural yellow color of the macaroni. The anomaly should be localized on the discolored spot area only
small-chip-around-edge: visible breakage or missing sections at the edges of the macaroni pieces. These chips or cracks can be seen as irregularities in the otherwise smooth cylindrical shape of the macaroni. The anomaly should be localized on the chipped edge area on the edge only
small-scratches: thin and shallow lines or abrasions running along the surface of the macaroni. The anomaly should be localized on the scratched area only

normal: the HC-SR04 Ultrasonic Sensor Module PCB includes 2 cylindrical metal-can transducers (Receiver and Transmitter) placed horizontally, a 4-pin header, and a rectangular silver crystal oscillator. The term 'pins' refers exclusively to the 4-pin header connectors.
bent: one or more of the 4-pin header connector pins being misaligned significantlty. The anomaly should be localized on the bent pin area only
melt: ccumulation of silver-colored solder material, usually appearing as blobs or excess spillover. The anomaly should be localized on the melted solder area only
missing: one or both cylindrical transducers or one or multiple pins are absent. The anomaly should be localized on the missing component area only
scratch: visible scratch lines on the pdb surface, specially in the PCB board. The anomaly should be localized on the scratched area only

normal: the HC-SR04 Ultrasonic Sensor Module PCB includes 3 integrated circuits (left: U3, center: U2, right: U1) with multiple pins, a 4-pin header (VCC, Trig, Echo, GND) centered at the edge, several SMD resistors and capacitors arrayed in rows around the ICs, and 4 circular mounting holes at the corners. The blue PCB has clear labels ('HC-SR04', U1, U2, U3, labeled resistors, and capacitors). The term 'pins' refers exclusively to the 4-pin header at the top edge.
bent: one or more of the 4-pin header connector pins being misaligned or bent away from their original straight position. The anomaly should be localized on the bent pin area only
melt: accumulation of silver-colored solder material, usually appearing as blobs or excess spillover. The anomaly should be localized on the melted solder area only
missing: a component such as pins, circuits, or resistors is visibly absent from the board. The anomaly should be localized on the missing component area only
scratch: visible scratch lines on the surface of the PCB board. The anomaly should be localized on the scratched area only

normal: includes 2 LEDs (transparent IR emitter and black IR receiver), a 3-pin header, an integrated circuit (U1), a blue potentiometer (3362) for sensitivity adjustment, and several SMD resistors and capacitors arrayed around the IC. The term 'pins' refers exclusively to the 3-pin header and white and black LEDs on the sides of the board.
bent: one of pins or LEDs in either sides of the board are visibly bent or misaligned. The anomaly should be localized on the bent area only
melt: accumulation of silver-colored solder material, characterized by silver-colored blobs or smears on the board. The anomaly should be localized on the melted area only
missing: certain components like resistors, capacitors, pins, or LEDs are absent. The anomaly should be localized on the missing component area only
scratch: visible scratch lines or marks on the surface of the PCB board. The anomaly should be localized on the scratched area only

normal: the TP4056 Lithium Battery Charging Module PCB includes a micro USB port at the left edge, 4 connection pads labeled IN+, IN-, BAT+, and BAT- at the corners, an integrated circuit (U1) near the bottom center with multiple pins, several SMD resistors and capacitors around the IC, and 2 LEDs (CHRG, DONE) indicating charging status near the center top. The blue PCB has clear labels for component positions and connections. Check for secure attachment and alignment of the USB port, IC, resistors, capacitors, and LEDs, straight and firmly soldered connection pads, and legible markings
extra: presence of an unwanted object, such as dirt, dust, or an extra circuit component, located on the PCB. The anomaly should be localized on the extra object only
missing: characterized by the absence of one or more essential components such as pins, circuits, or resistors. The anomaly should be localized on the missing component area only

normal: is uniformly shaped with smooth, intact edges and corners. Its surface is free of any scratches, chips, or uneven marks and lacks colored spots or blemishes
burnt: characterized by an orangish-brownish patch that appears scorched or burnt. The anomaly should be localized on the burnt patch area only
corner-and-edge-breakage: visible breakage or chipping, located around the corners or along the edges. The anomaly should be localized on the chipped edge or corner area only
different-colour-spot: characterized by a small, distinct dark spot on the fryum. The anomaly should be localized on the discolored spot area only
similar-colour-spot: characterized by a small, light-colored spot that blends closely with the fryum's natural hue. The anomaly should be localized on that similar-colour spot only
small-scratches: characterized by thin and shallow lines or abrasions running along the surface of the fryum. The anomaly should be localized on the scratched area only
stuck-together: characterized by two or more fryums being adhered to each other, forming clusters. The anomaly should be localized on the stuck area only
